summary: Kimberley C. Patton is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1986–1992). Her career includes posts as an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1991) and assistant professor at Harvard (~1991).

Specializing in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Kimiaki Tanaka studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford, and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, Beijing Center for Japanese Studies, Keio University, and Toga Meditation Village.

Kimmo Koskenniemi is a linguist who studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and as director of the BAULT research community (attested 2015).
Kin Cheung works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).
King Chung Lo is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Leipzig University under the supervision of Eli Franco (2009).
King Pong Chiu specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester under the doctoral supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).

Kirby Flower Smith was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist. After studying at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins under Gildersleeve, Warren, and Bloomfield, he served as a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and directed the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an Indologist who completed his studies at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.
Kisho Masanobu is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his master's studies at Kyoto University (~1973–1975) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 1987–1988).

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under traditional and academic teachers, including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, and Gopinath Bhattacharya, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the Fourth Higher School (1896, 1899–1909) and served as Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

Kiyoaki Okuda is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968–1973). He held posts as professor at International Buddhist University (attested 1993) and director of Shitennoji Kyogaku Kenkyujo (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at Otani University, studying under Enga Teramoto, and held positions at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Kojo Girls' Vocational School (1938).
Kiyoshi Miki was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida (~1917–1920). He later held academic posts at Otani University and Ryukoku University (~1924–1927).

Kiyoshi Okano is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University as an associate professor (attested 2002) and as a professor (attested 2013–2024).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Rissho University. He held posts at Rissho University (attested 1990, 2001) and the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

Kiyoshi Yabuuchi was an archaeologist, historian, and sinologist. He studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and later held academic posts at Kyoto University (~1944–1969) and Ryukoku University (~1969–1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar and sinologist educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, served as President of Tsurumi University, and held professorships at several other institutions.

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer, later holding positions at Hokkaido University (~1998–2004), Tohoku University (~2004–2023), and Toyo Bunko.

Kiyozo Kazama is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (under Tsuji and Kōzu) and the University of Vienna. He held faculty posts at Nagoya University (~1965–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1989), and Hosei University (~1989–1999).
